title: CYP2D6: metoprolol (1554/1555/1556) - risk analysis and dose recommendation of the Dutch Pharmacogenetics Working Group
authors: KNMP Pharmacogenetics Working Group (Royal Dutch Pharmacists Association)
journal: Royal Dutch Pharmacists Association (KNMP), Dutch Pharmacogenetics Working Group; literature search to 27 June 2022, Working Group decision of 12 September 2022; document distributed through ClinPGx (formerly PharmGKB)
funder: not stated; the risk-analysis document carries no funding statement.
result: CYP2D6 converts metoprolol to O-desmethylmetoprolol and alpha-hydroxymetoprolol, whose activity is negligible; the active S-enantiomer is metabolised to a lesser extent than the less active R-enantiomer. Dose adjustments were calculated from AUC, steady-state concentration or oral clearance: for 62 poor metabolisers in 11 studies the weighted mean calculated adjustment was a reduction to 19% of the normal dose (range 3% to 34%, median 18%), rounded to 25%; for 234 intermediate metabolisers in 12 studies a reduction to 51% (range 15% to 95%, median 44%), rounded to 50%; for 35 ultra-rapid metabolisers in 5 studies an increase to 247% (range 166% to 468%, median 219%), rounded to 250%. Recommendations: for intermediate and poor metabolisers, if a gradual reduction in heart rate is desired or symptomatic bradycardia occurs, use smaller steps in dose titration and prescribe no more than 50% or 25% of the standard dose respectively, and in other cases no action is required; for ultra-rapid metabolisers use the maximum dose for the indication as the target and, if effectiveness remains insufficient, raise the dose to 2.5 times the standard dose or select an alternative, bisoprolol or carvedilol in heart failure and atenolol or bisoprolol in other indications, bisoprolol and atenolol not being metabolised by CYP2D6. Evidence considered: a meta-analysis and most patient studies found a greater reduction in heart rate for intermediate and poor metabolisers but little or no effect on blood pressure; the single study that examined symptomatic bradycardia, in 11 poor and 15 intermediate metabolisers, found no significant effect; one study of 1036 Chinese patients aged 60 or older found, for 381 intermediate metabolisers against 651 normal metabolisers, higher discontinuation for intolerance (8.3% in normal metabolisers, 1.5-fold higher in intermediate metabolisers) and adjusted odds ratios of 1.37 (95% CI 1.05 to 1.79) for any adverse event and 1.60 (1.22 to 2.09) for cardiovascular adverse events. Pre-emptive genotyping before starting metoprolol is classified as potentially beneficial, with a clinical implication score of 0 out of 10; genotyping can be considered for an individual patient, and where the genotype is available the Working Group recommends adhering to the gene-drug guideline.
